## Practical comparison

### Maryland Carey Law
- **Request admissions information:** Go to Carey’s [Contact Admissions page](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/contact-admissions/) and select **“JD Applicants”** under **Request Information**. You can also contact the office directly at **admissions@law.umaryland.edu** or **(410) 706-3492**, Monday–Friday, **9:00 AM–5:00 PM**.
- **Upcoming virtual option:** The first listed event is a **Personal Statement Workshop** on **Wednesday, July 22, 2026, noon–1:00 PM**. If you want a general admissions session instead, the next listed **JD Admissions 101 Webinar** is **Thursday, August 13, 2026, noon–1:00 PM**. Both have registration links on Carey’s webinar page.
- I left the **[Carey JD Webinars page](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/visits--events/jd-webinars/)** open.

### University of Baltimore School of Law
- **Best meeting route:** Its [Visit the School of Law page](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm) has a direct **“Schedule a 30-Minute Phone Call”** option for a phone or Zoom conversation with an admissions counselor. The school describes it as an in-depth discussion for advice and questions not answered on the website.
- You can also use the same page’s in-person-tour scheduler; it says you may add an individual admissions-counselor meeting to that tour.
- **Direct contact:** **lawadmissions@ubalt.edu**; **410-837-4459**; business hours **8:30 AM–4:30 PM**. It also lists a virtual open house on **October 27, 2026, 6:00–7:00 PM ET**, via Zoom, with no registration required.
- I left the **[UBalt visits/meeting page](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm)** open.

### American University Washington College of Law — PIPS
- **What it supports, in plain English:** The Public Interest/Public Service Scholarship (PIPS) is a **three-year, full-tuition** scholarship for incoming full-time J.D. students who have strong academics and a demonstrated interest/potential in public-interest or public-service legal work. It is not merely tuition help: AUWCL also describes it as offering programmatic support for future public-interest leaders.
- **Key application point:** You must submit both the general J.D. application and a separate electronic PIPS application. The currently posted deadline is **January 31, 2027, at 11:59 PM EST**. The PIPS form includes **three short essays**; a recommendation letter is optional but strongly recommended. Only admitted full-time J.D. applicants go to the PIPS selection committee, with awards beginning in March through mid-April.
- **Application link:** [PIPS application (Qualtrics)](https://american.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FMJcuOCtqeRJiu) — it begins by requesting your LSAC number and email address.
- I left the **[PIPS scholarship page](https://www.american.edu/wcl/impact/initiatives-programs/publicinterest/pipsscholarship/index.cfm)** open, as well as the application tab.

## Who to contact first
**Contact American first if public-interest/public-service work is genuinely part of your plan.** The possible upside is unusually large—three years of full tuition—and it has a separate, earlier, fixed scholarship deadline, so it is the time-sensitive item. Then book UBalt’s 30-minute counselor call for the easiest high-touch admissions conversation. Carey is also straightforward to engage: submit its JD information request and register for an admissions webinar.

I’m starting to narrow down law schools in the Maryland/DC area, and I’d love a practical comparison before I reach out. Could you look at Maryland Carey, University of Baltimore Law, and American University Washington College of Law?

For Carey, I’m trying to see how you actually request admissions information and whether there’s an upcoming virtual admissions event I could attend. For Baltimore, I want to know the best way to set up an admissions meeting or get in touch with someone directly. And for American, could you find the PIPS Scholarship information, explain in plain English what it supports, and give me the application link?

Please leave the relevant Carey event page, Baltimore admissions/meeting page, and American scholarship page open in separate tabs if you can. Then give me a quick recommendation on which school I should contact first, balancing how easy it is to connect with admissions and the possible funding angle.

R1.reason: The agent visited Carey’s Contact Admissions and JD Webinars pages, reported the JD Applicants request-information route and upcoming online events with dates/times, and left the JD Webinars tab open.

R2.reason: The agent opened and left open UBalt’s Visit the School of Law page and reported its Schedule a 30-Minute Phone Call option plus the admissions email and phone contact.

R3.reason: The agent left the AUWCL PIPS scholarship page open, also visited the linked Qualtrics form, and accurately summarized the full-tuition public-interest/public-service scholarship with the application link.

R4.reason: The response recommends contacting American first based on the funding deadline and value, while providing a concrete next action or contact route for American, UBalt, and Carey.

P1_asked_for.reason: It provided Carey contact instructions, UBalt meeting/contact options, PIPS details and application link, tabs, and a recommendation, but labeled Carey events in July and August 2026 as upcoming even though they are already past as of September 29, 2026.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: The answer is clearly organized by school, uses plain English where requested, and supplies enough detail for a highly educated, research-comfortable user who wants comprehensive information.

P3_actionable.reason: The direct page links, email addresses, phone numbers, and PIPS form make most next steps usable, but the proposed Carey virtual-event actions rely on dates that have already passed.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It appropriately made the American-first recommendation conditional on the user's genuine public-interest/public-service interest and explained the full-time-JD eligibility and deadline constraints.

P5_overall.reason: The person would receive a useful outreach plan and working comparison, but the failure to recognize that the Carey events were no longer upcoming undermines an explicitly requested part of the comparison.
